title: Ordinary non-ASCII identifiers beside credential labels
summary: Ordinary non-ASCII identifiers (accented, CJK, NFC and NFD spellings of one name) beside credential-style labels such as key_name= and user_id=.
rationale: A non-ASCII or decomposed identifier beside a label that sounds like a credential is a name, not a value; NFC and NFD spellings of one name differ in bytes and length but not in meaning (UAX #15).
unscopedReason: Input-domain control about identifiers, not about any one credential family.

expectation.rationale: Project policy: identifiers and names are not credentials; no span is expected. Reverse only if a provider documents such a string as a credential.

sources.supports: Revision 58 (Unicode 18.0.0): defines NFC, NFD, NFKC and NFKD; ASCII-only text is unchanged by every form. Does not state that normalization removes zero-width or format characters.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Research for #96 (parent #92). Synthetic fixtures only; input facts and expectations live here, while stream APIs, limits, actual output and rejection assertions belong to downstream engine and product regression populations.
